title: An-Nur, the Light
tomorrow: Eli has a blank page and a deadline. who shows him the way?

lines: ENOUGH FOR THE NEXT FEW STEPS.
A LAMP, A GLASS, A STAR.
cards: A phone flashlight in a dark parking lot. It doesn't light the whole world, only enough for the next few steps, and that's enough to get to the car. Yesterday's question: a lamp, a glass, a star.
What is the light in that verse? It's in Surah an-Nur, the chapter named for light, and it stacks its pictures one inside another, like a set of nesting boxes, each one glowing.

teach.h: A NICHE, A LAMP, A GLASS, A STAR.
teach.b: In Pickthall's words: "Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth. The similitude of His light is as a niche wherein is a lamp. The lamp is in a glass. The glass is as it were a shining star."
So the answer: the light is God's own. The niche, the lamp and the glass are a similitude, a picture of it. Today's Name is An-Nur, the Light.
Here's a detail to tell a friend tonight.

teach.h: NEITHER EAST NOR WEST. LIGHT UPON LIGHT.
teach.b: The verse says the lamp is lit from a blessed olive tree, neither of the east nor of the west, whose oil almost glows before any fire touches it. Then come three words: light upon light. Now a neighbor.

teach.h: PSALMS: A LAMP UNTO MY FEET.
teach.b: Jews and Christians pray a line from the Psalms, in the King James words: "Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path." That's shared, and it's close: a lamp in the dark, from God, enough for the next step.
And the honest difference. In the Psalm, the lamp is God's word, lighting the road. In Surah an-Nur, Light is a Name of God Himself, and the lamp is only the picture.
Christians also hear Jesus say, in John's Gospel, "I am the light of the world"; Muslims honor Jesus as a prophet and keep the Name An-Nur for God alone.
Neither has to dim the other.

how: Muslims recite 24:35, known as the Verse of Light; al-Ghazali wrote a whole book on it, the Niche of Lights.

o: the Light of the heavens and earth
the Morning Star, a sign before dawn
the Fire that guided Moses at night

games.q: lamps inside lamps — tap the pairs.
p: as it were a shining star

s: 24:35 says the lamp is literally God
it's a similitude: His light is like a lamp in a niche.
a Psalm calls God's word a lamp unto my feet
"Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path."
in 24:35 the olive tree is neither of the east nor of the west
its oil almost glows before any fire touches it: light upon light.

games.q: a friend from church says: 'my Bible calls God's word a lamp. your Qur'an says God is light. so we believe exactly the same thing, right?' what's the honest reply?
o: we share the lamp in the dark; what the lamp is differs a little.
yes, exactly the same; every faith teaches one identical idea.
no, nothing in common; your book's light isn't the real light.
games.why: Psalm 119:105 and 24:35 share the picture of God's light for the path. in one the lamp is God's word; in the other, Light is God's Name. shared, and different, ranked by no one.

practice: Find one light near you: a lamp, a window, a screen turned down low. Look at it, then let your eyes soften so you notice what it touches, the edges and faces it makes visible.
Rest your eyes there for the sit, and let the light do its quiet work.

wordCard.voice: An-Nur. The Light of the heavens and the earth: the lamp and the glass are pictures; the light is His. Light upon light.

orig.note: Arabic: the Light, a Name of Allah from 24:35, in the surah of the same name.
